sections.title: Ultimatum, transit and provisioning
sections.text: Withdrawal correspondence combines evacuation deadlines, transit negotiations and provisioning requests.

entries.title: The Romanian ultimatum in the evening report
entries.summary: The Romanian evacuation ultimatum remains unanswered in this evening report. Its relative deadline cannot be securely assigned a calendar date.

entries.title: Instructions for movement through Hungary
entries.summary: The message reports Hungarian armistice negotiations, says German troops are to leave Hungarian and South Slav territory, and requests instructions for the two staff officers AOK11 is to send.

entries.title: Arad provisions: 80,000 men and 30,000 animals
entries.summary: Provision trains are requested for Arad, with action through the Hungarian government. Independent receptions supply missing text and support the reported strength figures.

sections.title: Transport and medical provision
sections.text: Railway planning and medical transport recommendations specify supplies and accommodation for returning personnel.

entries.title: Transit planning under armistice conditions
entries.summary: A report cites Hungarian newspapers allowing fifteen days for transit, considers holding the 11th Army on the Danube, and requests the actual agreement.

entries.title: Heated sick wagons and medical return transport
entries.summary: The recommendations specify heated sick wagons, cooking equipment and hot tea for return transports from Turkey.

entries.title: Requests for provisions during withdrawal
entries.summary: Separate messages request the applicable armistice conditions and a provisions train to Szolnok on the Theiss.

sections.title: Command, internment and unrest
sections.text: Mackensen’s appeal and the Berlin council’s letter address internment. The Kiev report concerns neutrality during impending unrest.

entries.title: Mackensen’s appeal against internment
entries.summary: After Berthelot communicates Foch’s position, Mackensen challenges the demand for disarmament and internment and describes provisioning difficulties.

entries.title: Internment correspondence
entries.summary: The Berlin council tells Mackensen’s soldiers’ council that the Entente insists on internment and would regard maintaining the departure order as a breach of the armistice.

entries.title: Kiev unrest and soldiers’ council neutrality
entries.summary: The conditional reading warns of impending unrest between the Hetman government and a named opponent and reports the soldiers’ council’s decision for neutrality. Petljura remains a separately priced name proposal.

sections.title: Cargo, loading and release
sections.text: Cargo reports accompany requests concerning loading, release and onward transport.

entries.title: Nikolaev supply cargo and shipping decisions
entries.summary: A report describes steamers entering Nikolaev and goods remaining aboard under military guard, and asks how the recipient intends to proceed.

entries.title: Tobacco awaiting loading at Poti
entries.summary: Tobacco is reported ready at Poti; the sender asks when loading will be possible.

entries.title: An inquiry about releasing oil
entries.summary: The sender asks whether Izzet Pasha’s renewed order to release oil has succeeded.

sections.title: Ship sales, payment and authority
sections.text: Ship-sale correspondence addresses payment, title and crewing. A separate order sets out naval armistice instructions.

entries.title: Corcovado sale terms, payment and transfer of title
entries.summary: Proposed terms allocate seizure and nonpayment risks and restrict resale. A separate report describes Turkish crewing; a later order halts an unsettled sale or outstanding transfer of title and gives cash payment in Germany as the condition to state to Turkey.

entries.title: Turkish tonnage purchases and authorization
entries.summary: The Marineamt discourages sales except in extreme necessity, requires authorization and immediate payment, and questions whether Turkish buyers intend to transport Germans.

entries.title: Naval armistice instructions
entries.summary: The order directs immediate forwarding, cessation of hostilities at noon on 11 November 1918 and assembly of naval forces at their bases.

sections.title: Cash supply and denominations
sections.text: Cash requests specify delivery routes and banknote denominations as well as amounts.

entries.title: Thirty million crowns requested for wages and purchases
entries.summary: The request specifies a giant aircraft to Brasso and both large and small notes for wages and purchases in Hungary.

entries.title: One million crowns daily by ordinary aircraft
entries.summary: The proposed daily airlift alternates between Kronstadt and Hermannstadt. The interrupted ending concerns small banknotes.

entries.title: The complete small-banknote instruction
entries.summary: The full reception restores the request for notes as small as possible and corrects an earlier conjecture about the interrupted copy.

sections.title: Remittance, payout and guarded transport
sections.text: Bank transfers, local payouts and guarded transport appear as distinct administrative operations.

entries.title: An initial five-million-crown transfer through Vienna
entries.summary: The message announces a transfer by the Wiener Bankverein to Kronstadt in mixed denominations and asks whether local payout succeeded and was sufficient.

entries.title: A guarded rail alternative for Hermannstadt cash
entries.summary: If the Döberitz aircraft has not departed, cash is to travel under special guard by train through Szolnok and Arad to Hermannstadt, with arrival notices.

entries.title: Arad advances and partial crown remittances
entries.summary: An Arad request asks about access to an advance; a separate message reports partial crown remittances and a severe banknote shortage. Their transactions cannot be equated.

sections.title: Procurement cancellation and resale
sections.text: Paid consignments, outstanding contracts and stranded goods receive different treatment in the procurement orders.

entries.title: Purchase stop-orders and the paid-consignment exception
entries.summary: Stop-orders halt further buying and loading. A separate instruction permits loading paid consignments, cancels other contracts and requests Westernhagen’s return.

entries.title: Local resale of silk when transport is uncertain
entries.summary: Silk and related Caucasus purchases are to be resold locally where removal cannot be assured. Parallel receptions establish the complete disposal instruction.

entries.title: The Odessa wagon-sale request
entries.summary: An Odessa-routed request seeks the best possible terms for selling wagon Magdeburg 9910. The damaged adjacent phrase does not securely identify its contents.

sections.title: Allowances and currency redemption
sections.text: The correspondence addresses subsistence allowances, banknote redemption and reported currency prices.

entries.title: Military allowance instructions
entries.summary: The message calls for lower cash meal allowances, communal purchasing and food in kind, and rejects a cost-of-living supplement.

entries.title: Negotiations over stamped and unstamped lei notes
entries.summary: The sender seeks amounts, denominations and stamping details for lei redemption and proposes bank arrangements. Negotiations and several exchange-rate values remain unresolved.

entries.title: Ruble prices and payments above par
entries.summary: The conditional reading reports 140 marks per 100 Tsar rubles in Kiev and up to 190 in Warsaw, and recommends payments above par for BONS if necessary.

sections.title: Schedules, retransmission and wire connections
sections.text: Service inquiries concern transmission periods, substitute stations and wire connections.

entries.title: Eilvese listening and transmission periods
entries.summary: The telegram specifies Eilvese sending and receiving arrangements and provisional transmission windows; numerical assignments and unstated units remain qualified.

entries.title: NKJ backup and relay arrangements
entries.summary: Repeated messages ask which station could replace NKJ during interruption and whether NKJ relays Mackensen traffic. Sevastopol is proposed as a backup.

entries.title: Wire communications and Braila–Tiraspol return instructions
entries.summary: Related receptions discuss wire communications, instructions for the Ackermann post to return from Braila, and a Tiraspol continuation.

sections.title: Cipher instructions and service procedure
sections.text: Ringbahn instructions extend the use of November keys; the September orders regulate listening and acknowledgments.

entries.title: The Tiflis Ringbahn instruction
entries.summary: The instruction retains November Ringbahn keys for December use, starting with the 10 November key on 1 December 1918.

entries.title: Instructions to reuse Ringbahn keys
entries.summary: November Ringbahn keys are to be retained and the December key postponed. The continuation schedules reuse through 21 December 1918.

entries.title: September radio-service procedure
entries.summary: Daily listening instructions accompany a separate request to send radiograms during reception of the Nauen press and postpone acknowledgments until afterward.

sections.title: Vehicles, equipment and departures
sections.text: Departure arrangements combine vehicle allocation, equipment movement and continued station service.

entries.title: Trucks, trailers, readiness and the Hanau destination
entries.summary: Truck and trailer messages concern readiness, departure arrangements and Hanau as a destination. A truck-departure report says the sender plans to remain with a number of men until Sunday; timings remain incomplete.

entries.title: Loading apparatus and keeping the station ready
entries.summary: Parallel orders send two US apparatuses toward Darmstadt while retaining station readiness, and select the best trailer for loading with a petrol pump held ready.

entries.title: Station control and Seifert’s arrival and departure messages
entries.summary: Station reports describe soldiers’ council supervision, continued operation and custody of cipher keys. Separate messages concern Seifert’s movements and immediate listening instructions.

entries.title: Arrival, departure and car inquiries on 12 November 1918
entries.summary: Short messages report arrival and departure, request notice when Seifert arrives, and ask where the car is. Repeated texts do not establish additional journeys.

entries.title: Postponed departure, supper inquiry and farewell
entries.summary: Distinct service messages postpone a departure, ask for a headcount for a warm evening meal, and convey a farewell.

sections.title: Civilian residence, travel and discharge
sections.text: These requests concern civilian residence, travel after recovery and release from military service.

entries.title: German civilians in Constantinople
entries.summary: An inquiry concerns German civilians, especially women and children, their whereabouts and permission to remain in Turkey. It reports that transport through Ukraine is unavailable.

entries.title: Kremp’s request for a departure date
entries.summary: Kremp reports recovery and asks the Constantinople military mission’s transport section to specify his departure date.

entries.title: Rudolf’s discharge request
entries.summary: The military mission is asked to discharge an embassy-attached serviceman whose name appears as Rudolf Rudolf.

sections.title: Transfers, recalls and medical recovery
sections.text: Personnel orders assign or cancel postings; the medical report gives treatment and recovery as grounds for transfer.

entries.title: The Breslau staff transfer
entries.summary: The order assigns Major Strzemieczny to special employment with the VI Army Corps command at Breslau, under the documented historical identification.

entries.title: Recalls of military-mission personnel
entries.summary: The orders cancel Siegfried’s and Osthoff’s assignments to Turkey and the military mission; Osthoff is to be transferred to a railway regiment’s replacement battalion. Both say the cabinet order will follow.

entries.title: Treatment and recovery at a replacement unit
entries.summary: The two parts report transfer to a replacement unit for specialist medical treatment and recovery.

sections.title: Mission staffing, equipment and procurement
sections.text: Appointments and procurement exchanges cover reinforcement, market information, equipment and suspended purchases.

entries.title: October correspondence with the Caucasus
entries.summary: Messages concern administrative reinforcement, purchasing and prices, electrical equipment, Violetta cargo for Poti, radio arrangements and liaison with Tiflis.

entries.title: Officer replacements and manganese purchases
entries.summary: Officer-reassignment messages name a Bavarian cavalry-brigade appointment and a replacement for the Caucasus delegation. A separate instruction suspends further manganese purchases.

entries.title: Market intelligence and an inspector request
entries.summary: Westernhagen is urged to return with local market information before buying begins. Another fragment concerns an inspector request with Kress’s agreement.

sections.title: Representation, Poti traffic and withdrawal
sections.text: Polish representation, Poti horse transport and withdrawal conditions are documented in separate exchanges.

entries.title: Polish representation in Tiflis
entries.summary: The Polish Foreign Ministry appoints Waclaw von Ostrowski representative for Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, based in Tiflis; the courier identification remains conditional.

entries.title: Poti horse shipment and handover
entries.summary: The partly reconstructed opening concerns horses aboard steamers toward Poti. Later parts include a cavalry-brigade shipment, an incomplete horse-handover clause and an urgent request for a reply.

entries.title: Allied conditions for withdrawal and the Tiflis guard
entries.summary: Parallel receptions explain that Allied assessment of local conditions governs withdrawal from former Russian territory; no demand to remove the Tiflis guard had yet been received.

secondary.title: Unresolved sources
secondary.text: Seven physical sources have no accepted body reading. Their page editions preserve the received text and current research.
